garrulous

GAIR-uh-lus · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Garrulous is excessively talkative, especially about unimportant matters, in a rambling way.

The garrulous neighbor kept the mail carrier on the porch for twenty minutes every single day.

Example

Once the garrulous barber started talking, customers knew their haircut would take twice as long as anywhere else in town.

Garrulous describes talkativeness that rambles on past the point anyone wants to keep listening.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

chatty: Chatty means talkative in a light, friendly way -- pleasant small talk that both people enjoy. Garrulous talk has lost that welcome quality: it rambles on about unimportant things long after the listener wants it to stop.

rambling: Rambling describes talk that wanders without a clear point, but it says nothing about how much of it there is. Garrulous adds sheer quantity: a garrulous person pours out that wandering talk constantly, until listeners are worn down.

loquacious: Loquacious means talking a great deal in a fluent, confident way, and it can even sound admiring. Garrulous is the tiresome cousin: the same flood of words, but aimless and rambling, offered whether or not anyone wants to hear it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

taciturn: reluctant to speak much

reticent: reserved and uncommunicative

Where it sits · how tiresome the chatter gets

talkative → garrulous → insufferable

talkative vs. garrulous: Talkative is a plain, everyday word for liking to talk; garrulous adds a tiresome, rambling quality that can wear on a listener.

insufferable vs. garrulous: Insufferable chatter goes a step beyond garrulous: garrulous talk wears listeners down but they politely put up with it, while insufferable talk is so tiresome that no one can bear to stay and listen.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — garr: to chatter (Latin (garrire, imitative))

suffix — -ulous: full of, inclined to (Latin)

Put it together: garr- ('to chatter') + -ulous ('full of') together give the sense of chattering excessively.

Use the root in a new word: garrulity: Cousin Leo's garrulity made the four-hour drive to the lake feel twice as long.
